subjects.displayTitle: The twin Manifestations: recognition and relationship
subjects.introduction: He is My Beloved and I am His Beloved, Bahá’u’lláh says of the Báb, adding that the Báb spoke only in praise of Him and He speaks only in praise of the Báb. The bond between the two Manifestations is first of all a love, each bearing witness to the other, and only then a doctrine. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá states the doctrine plainly: the Báb is at once a Manifestation of the oneness of God and the Forerunner of Bahá’u’lláh, which unsettles any tidy division between messenger and herald. John the Baptist, calling himself a voice preparing the way, offers a familiar picture of witness and recognition, but John said he was not the Christ, and the analogy stops where the Báb’s own station begins [1]. A second distinction runs alongside and should not be confused with the first: within each Manifestation there is a station of unity, in which the voice is God’s, and a station of distinction, in which He speaks as servant. One sun appears in two mirrors, and each mirror keeps its individuality. The journey continues toward the Báb and the Primal Point, the station and claims the Báb made for Himself, and the person of Bahá’u’lláh.
subjects.arc: Begin with mutual love, distinguish the two missions, explore unity and station, then consider recognition and service.

order.why: Establish the Báb’s two roles and Bahá’u’lláh’s station.
shortened: This is the foundation of the belief of the people of Baha (may my life be offered up for them): "His Holiness, the Exalted One (the Bab), is the Manifestation of the Unity and Oneness of God and the Forerunner of the Ancient Beauty. His Holiness the Abha Beauty (may my life be a sacrifice for His steadfast friends) is the Supreme Manifestation of God and the Dayspring of His Most Divine Essence. All others are servants unto Him and do His bidding."

order.why: Open with mutual remembrance, praise and love.
Distinguish the unity of revelation from particular missions and voices.
shortened: We have already in the foregoing pages assigned two stations unto each of the Luminaries arising from the Daysprings of eternal holiness. One of these stations, the station of essential unity, We have already explained. "No distinction do We make between any of them." The other is the station of distinction, and pertaineth to the world of creation and to the limitations thereof. In this respect, each Manifestation of God hath a distinct individuality, a definitely prescribed mission, a predestined Revelation, and specially designated limitations.

order.why: Consider the contrast between personal lowliness and revealed power.
Read the two relationships expressed by divine and human speech.
shortened: When I contemplate, O my God, the relationship that bindeth me to Thee, I am moved to proclaim to all created things "verily I am God!"; and when I consider my own self, lo, I find it coarser than clay!

order.why: Explore the language of relationship to God.
shortened: Men have failed to perceive Our purpose in the references We have made to Divinity and Godhood.

The Seal of the Prophets -- may the souls of all else but Him be offered up for His sake -- saith: "Manifold are Our relationships with God. At one time, We are He Himself, and He is We Ourself. At another He is that He is, and We are that We are."

order.why: Hear the Báb’s distinction between the two stations.
Keep transcendence beside the Manifestation’s twofold station.
Read unity together with distinctions among the Messengers.
Use the mirror image to consider sameness and difference.
shortened: Thus, should the mirrored Sun proclaim, 'I am the Sun!' this is but truth; and should It cry, 'I am not the Sun!' this is the truth as well.

order.why: Read the same sun in individual mirrors.
shortened: The Manifestations of God are like so many different mirrors, as They each have Their own distinct individuality, but that which is reflected in these mirrors is one and the same sun.

order.why: Distinguish the spiritual orb from its radiance.
shortened: Question: "And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come."

Answer: The sanctified realities of the Manifestations of God have two spiritual stations: One is that of the state of divine manifestation, which can be compared to the orb of the sun, and the other is that of radiance and revelation, which may be likened to the divine light and perfections--the Holy Spirit.

order.why: Hear the further distinction of physical and spiritual stations.
Return to the Báb’s image of the sun of unity.
Widen the view to the varied patterns of revelation.
shortened: It must be evident to thee that the divine Cause, the celestial Will, and the heavenly Purpose have never been confined by limitations. In some ages there hath been a single Soul, and in other times multiple Temples have appeared from the Dayspring of the Cause, as is recorded and evident in all the Books of old and recent times.

And if in certain utterances of the Manifestations of the Cause and holy Dawning-places thou perceivest limitation to one, be not veiled thereby but consider the origin of the divine Tree and holy Sapling, for the Cause of God hath ever appeared and shall ever appear without limit or number.

order.why: Consider a shared purpose through different names.
shortened: O dear one! All nations await two Manifestations, and these two Manifestations signify the Blessed Beauty (i.e. Baha'u'llah) and His Holiness the Bab. Words are different, but the purpose is one. One has called Him "Mahdi" and another hath called Him "Christ". One hath named the Blessed Beauty (i.e. Baha'ullah) the "Lord of Hosts" and another hath called Him the "Heavenly Father".

order.why: See both Manifestations as guiding lights.
shortened: Ye have been illumined by the guiding light of the glad tidings emanating from the morning brightness of the Bab, may my spirit be a sacrifice to His exalted holiness. And ye have received a generous portion from the effulgent rays of the loving providence of the great Luminary of the Concourse on High, the Abha Beauty Himself.

order.why: Keep the absence of an outward meeting beside spiritual identity.
Read the covenant expressed through praise of the Bayán.
Hear the Báb’s declaration concerning the One to come.
Consider the herald’s announcement in the image of circling the throne.
shortened: This is the Primal Point, Who circles round the Throne and proclaims with His most exalted call: "O my people! This is He Whom I gave you glad tidings of in the Books of God and what the All-Merciful revealed in the Furqan through His words 'the Day when thy Lord cometh, or some of the signs of thy Lord,' if ye be of those who know.

order.why: Read the transition from announcement to fulfillment.
shortened: He it was Whom Thou hast determined to be the Herald of Thy Most Great Revelation and the Announcer of Thy Most Ancient Splendor.
And when Thy promise came to pass and the set time was fulfilled, He Who is the Possessor of all Names and Attributes was made manifest unto men.

order.why: Hear the First and Last in the language of beauty.
Read the change of name through the claim of return.
shortened: Leave behind what thou hast and take what hath been sent down unto thee from the One mighty in His Cause, Who hath appeared and proclaimed: "Verily, He appeared once by the name of 'Ali, then by this name in His final return."

order.why: Preserve the distinctive names in this proclamation.
shortened: Say: Verily He appeared aforetime under the name of 'Ali before Nabil, and in this Revelation under the name of Husayn before 'Ali.

order.why: Hear the successive appearances named in the passage.
shortened: Verily, He appeared by the name of Ali in the first time, then by the name of Husayn in another time.

order.why: Consider the continuity of command.
shortened: He has come as 'Ali came from the heaven of the Cause with manifest sovereignty, and He commands you but what 'Ali commanded before.

order.why: Read acknowledgment of the Later as acknowledgment of the First.
Retain the statement concerning the subsequent Manifestation.
shortened: Say: Verily He appeared once in the name of 'Ali, and this is His subsequent manifestation, whereat all who are in the heavens and on earth were struck with terror, save them whom God preserved through His grace, and unto Him shall all things return both in the latter and former times.

order.why: Read the sequence of names in its scriptural language.
Recounts an intermediary’s historical connection with the Bab and Baha’u’llah.
Keep the dream’s interpretation within its symbolic setting.
Read the relation between the Qá’im and Qayyúm.
shortened: The Qayyum hath appeared after the Qa'im and hath arisen to the Cause with a sovereignty before which all who are in the heavens and on earth shall bow down, as attesteth the Book of God, the Mighty, the Wise.

order.why: Introduce the interpretation of the promised figures.
shortened: Time and again it has flowed from the pen of 'Abdu'l-Baha and has been explicitly and conclusively declared that what is meant in the prophecies by the Lord of Hosts and the Promised Christ is the Blessed Beauty and the Exalted One [the Bab], and the beliefs of all must be centered on this explicit and conclusive text.

order.why: Keep the explanation of two expected figures together.
shortened: All the Scriptures have foretold the advent of two Manifestations, even as the Gospel doth refer to the coming of Elijah and the Messiah, by which is meant the Bab and Baha'u'llah. There is no third Manifestation.

order.why: Read the comparisons across scriptures as Bahá’í interpretations.
shortened: All the peoples of the world are awaiting two Manifestations, Who must be contemporaneous. This is what they all have been promised. In the Torah the Jews are promised the Lord of Hosts and the Messiah. In the Gospel, the return of Christ and Elijah is foretold. In the religion of Muhammad there is the promise of the Mahdi and the Messiah.

order.why: Hear the reported appeal to the expectations of earlier communities.
Read the reported interpretation of changing garments and celestial imagery.
shortened: The Reality of God in them never varies; only the garment in which the Primal Reality is clothed is different according to the time and place of their Appearance and Declaration to the world. One Day it is the garment of Abraham, then Moses, then Jesus, then Baha'u'llah.

The Manifestations are as suns in the Heaven of the Divine Will. Sometimes the sun and moon are far apart; for instance, in the middle of month they are 180 degrees from each other. But in the beginning and end of the lunar month they are only one degree apart.
In the Qur'an Muhammad prophesied that in this Day the Sun and Moon will meet in Heaven; that is, the spiritual Sun and Moon of this Dispensation will rise together in the form of man.

order.why: Consider the concentration of prophetic expectation.
Read the claim that proofs are centered in the two.
Hear the reported account of two Manifestations in this period.
shortened: December 1---In this greatest period there are only two manifestations, the blessed Bab (May my soul be a ransom to him!) and the Manifestation of the Blessed Perfection (Glory be to Him!).

order.why: Keep the reported distinction between glad tidings and fulfillment.
Preserve the polemical passage in its own symbolic terms.
Read the warning concerning rejection of both appearances.
shortened: Those denied God when He appeared with the name of 'Ali in truth, and these have denied Him when He appeared once again with this Name, at which all who are in the heavens and earth were struck with terror.

order.why: Distinguish ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s servitude from their stations.
shortened: The second obligation is to establish the oneness of the invisible Beauty of Abha and the perfect divine Manifestation of the Primal Point and the pure, absolute, essential, inner, true, explicit servitude of 'Abdu'l-Baha without any trace of mention other than that.

order.why: Keep the reported dawn and sun analogy with its explicit limit.
Read the observer’s report of modesty in that light.
Connect recognition with service to both Manifestations.
shortened: So blessed are you and I, both of whom entered under the shadow of servitude to His Holiness the Herald (may my spirit be sacrificed for Him) and His Holiness the Abha Beauty (may my being be sacrificed for His luminous threshold).

order.why: Close the linked passages with believers who heard both calls.
Retain the supplied provisional explanation of differing perspectives.
Read the supplied distinction of function and essence.
Close with the supplied account of the Báb’s distinctive twofold role.

questions: How does mutual praise deepen your understanding of the relationship between the Báb and Bahá’u’lláh?
What changes when the Báb is understood both as a Manifestation and as a herald?
How do the images of sun and mirror preserve individuality within unity?
How would you distinguish the relationship between the two Manifestations from the two stations discussed within each?
What does John’s testimony clarify about preparation and recognition, and where does the comparison cease to fit?
Which passage invites you to explore the writings or particular mission of either Manifestation more closely?

references.label: 1 · John 1:19–34 · The witness and the one announced
references.note: John identifies himself as a voice preparing the way and bears witness to Jesus. Compare the acts of announcement and recognition with the passages concerning the Báb. John expressly says he is not the Christ; the compilation identifies the Báb as a Manifestation in his own right as well as a forerunner. That difference limits the analogy even where its language of witness is illuminating.

subjects.introduction: Knowledge that a neighbour is hungry feeds no one. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá presses the point: a friend who learns that another has no food for the evening should neither rest nor sleep until food is found. Charitable associations are what happens when that urgency refuses to depend on chance. Funds for orphans with members of every faith, relief societies in a famine, travel money redirected to the poor, a village’s organized provision for need, endowments and scholarships: each turns sympathy into an arrangement that can be trusted. Around the House of Worship, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá envisions hospitals, schools and shelters, so that worship and welfare grow from one root, and he laughs at the question whether charity is advisable: give to the poor, for words leave their pockets no fuller. In Acts, neglected widows prompt a community to appoint people responsible for daily distribution, a reminder that someone is always being overlooked [1]. The journey leads on into generosity as a quality of soul, into service to others, and into the institution that gathers prayer and practical care under one roof.
subjects.arc: Begin with hunger and response, widen the circle of care, examine organization and stewardship, and end with shared responsibility.

order.why: Bring the need close through the hungry neighbor.
shortened: The aim is this, that the friends of God must assist each other, and in assistance be greater than all the other communities of the world. If ones of the friends find out that another has no food for this evening, for instance, he should not rest, he should not sleep till he finds food for him.

order.why: Open with the reported difference between knowing and feeding.
shortened: To know that to reach a state of perfection is possible is good, to march forward on the path is better. We know that to help the poor and to be merciful is good and pleases God, but knowledge alone does not feed the starving man, nor can the poor be warmed by knowledge or words, in the bitter winter.

order.why: Extend care to friend and stranger.
shortened: O servant of God! Regarding the charitable funds from the endowments of your late grandfather about which you wrote - distribute these among the poor, weak, disabled and orphans, whether friend or stranger.

order.why: Read an association serving orphans across religious boundaries.
Hear the reported inclusion of every color and race.
Keep the urgency of children facing hunger.
Read assistance in a particular famine.
shortened: Praise be to God that during the time of famine, scarcity, hardship and tribulation, the Society for the Aid of the Poor showed forth effort and rendered assistance, and the poor among the friends remained patient, thankful and dignified.

order.why: Hear the reported call to attend to suffering.
shortened: The poor of this world suffer: we should care for them.

order.why: Consider redirecting unused travel provisions to humanity.
shortened: I was very pleased with the friends for showing such resolve, and I accepted, but since travel provisions are ready and nothing is needed, therefore I desire that the divine friends spend these amounts on charitable works for the general benefit of humanity on my behalf. This matter is very important.

order.why: Read the preference for assisting the poor over travel expense.
Introduce an association’s purpose and service.
Hear encouragement for a charitable society.
shortened: Regarding the Charitable Society about which thou didst write - you must certainly support this society and encourage it. Do not let it cease or weaken. Rather, the loved ones of God must strive with heart and soul so that day by day this society may gain strength and engage in service to the Cause - educating children, nurturing orphans, helping the poor, spreading knowledge, and becoming a means of guiding people.

order.why: Read the aim of bringing comfort to all.
shortened: Likewise the charitable association meeting - this is very beneficial and brings comfort to souls of every kind.

order.why: Connect gatherings with practical benefit and children’s care.
shortened: In the gathering of fellowship, the discussions must be confined to beneficial matters, namely: the exaltation of the Word of God, promotion of the teachings of God, education of souls, instruction of children, protection and nurturing of orphans, assistance to the weak and poor, support of the disabled, promotion of charitable works and benevolent causes.

order.why: Consider a village’s organized provision for need and public services.
Read the proposal for pooled resources and enduring income.
Keep the named relief effort’s instructions for trusted stewardship.
shortened: You have taken up a good occupation which deserves praise, for helping the poor and orphans is service to the Kingdom of God and no righteous deed has been or is greater than this. However, if you could assist the poor of Syria it would be more acceptable, and this should be done through a trustworthy person among the friends like Kalim, because when committees in those regions send aid through committees in these regions, most of the funds sent are kept by the committees here and very little reaches the poor. But if you send it through the friends, all of it reaches the poor.

order.why: Connect an assembly with food distribution.
shortened: Blessed is the Spiritual Assembly for having prepared some food for distribution among the poor and weak. Let those who act, act likewise.

order.why: Preserve the particular referral concerning an assembly.
shortened: Regarding what thou hadst written about the selection of the assembly for charitable affairs and benevolent works, refer to his honor Afnan of the Divine Lote-Tree.

order.why: Consider protection and order within an association.
shortened: Regarding the charitable company you wrote about, this charitable company must be protected and preserved, and complete order must be strived for.

order.why: Read the account of a disciples’ fund in its own setting.
Hear the reported use of community resources for a deceased person’s debts.
Consider printing proceeds directed to charity.
Read the practical example of honey production.
Keep the counsel concerning particular proceeds and wisdom.
shortened: And if it would not be outside of wisdom in another instance, spend its proceeds by order of the Center of the Covenant on orphans and the poor and weak.

order.why: Connect a charitable institution with children and learning.
shortened: O divine friends! The Charitable Society is among the institutions of the Lord of creation, for it cares for orphans and ensures comfort for the poor, weak and needy among mankind, and is a means for teaching children and promoting the Cause of the All-Merciful.

order.why: Read the Hamadan effort for relief and education.
shortened: Your letter hath come and hath occasioned the utmost joy, with its news that, praised be God, in Hamadan a welfare and relief association hath been established. I trust that this will become a source of general prosperity and assistance, and that means will be provided to set the hearts of the poor and weak at rest, and to educate the orphans and other children.

order.why: Follow scholarships across national boundaries.
shortened: The Western friends have rendered a worthy service to the Tarbiat School through the instrumentality of the Orient-Occident Unity in Washington.

It is hoped that this channel of philanthropy will be continually widened, its various interests solidified, its annual scholarships kept up and increased in number, and its wholesome, disinterested influence expanded.

order.why: Consider voluntary educational support between Iran and America.
shortened: In America, a company has been established under the name of the Iran-America Educational Society, and papers concerning this have been sent by Mirza Ahmad and are being forwarded to Aqa Mirza Ali-Akbar.
Now if the American friends wish, of their own accord and with willing hearts, to make a contribution to the Tarbiyat School, this will increase the connection.

order.why: Read generosity in an educational association.
Introduce the social dependencies of the House of Worship.
Hear the reported list of institutions of service.
Read the reported provision for varied forms of vulnerability.
Keep the reported plans for education and shelter.
Consider the reported relation between the center and its dependencies.
Connect their administration with love in the reported account.
shortened: On another part of it there will be a home for the incurables. In still another part there will be a home for the poor. In still another part there will be a home for orphans. All these will be administered with love.

order.why: Read the hope that one foundation will encourage others.
Praises philanthropy, education and the alleviation of suffering.
Consider a firm basis for contributions and action.
Keep the reported description of historical endowments.
Read the historical report of Tiberias and overseas assistance in context.
Hear the reported famine assistance extending beyond fellow believers.
Read cooperation with beneficial movements.
Consider reported appreciation of philanthropic organizations.
shortened: Their disgrace was changed into glory and they were everywhere esteemed and revered. They organized many Societies, laid the foundation of many philanthropic institutions and became famous for their charitable deeds.

order.why: Hear the reported recognition of societies working for human betterment.
Consider the reported relation between wealth, community and happiness.
Read the reported disappointment of wealth without generosity.
shortened: Therefore it became evident that the end of the people of wealth is disappointment after disappointment; except those rich persons who expend their money in charitable affairs and dispense their wealth on philanthropic channels. Such blessed souls like unto the brilliant stars will shine from the horizon of Everlasting Glory.

order.why: Keep the reported encouragement to give.
Hear the reported range of institutions serving need.
shortened: As to general protection, the believers are enjoined to look after one another.
Another is the getting ready of hospitals, dispensaries, home for cripples, schools for educating orphans, etc.

order.why: Read the reported image of aid as water to thirsty ground.
Return to charity toward wayfarers and the poor.
Preserve the Báb’s particular counsel concerning land and assistance.
Hear a prayer for philanthropic endeavor.
shortened: I beg of God that these philanthropic aims of yours may play a great effect in this world.
I hope that through the power of the love of Baha’u’llah thou mayest put into execution the philanthropic aims and promote the Teachings of Baha’u’llah.

order.why: Consider charitable action through the language of healing.
Read the encouragement addressed to a healing society.
Close with the reported image of benevolence as an outpouring.

questions: What turns sympathy for another person into dependable assistance?
Which passages widen the circle of care beyond familiar friends or communities?
What arrangements help a charitable fund remain trustworthy and responsive to real needs?
How does the relationship between worship and social institutions affect your idea of a community’s spiritual life?
What can the neglected widows in Acts teach about discovering gaps in an existing system of care?
Where might a modest, sustained effort make a meaningful difference in your own setting?

references.label: 1 · Acts 6:1–7 · Responding to neglected widows
references.note: A complaint that Greek-speaking widows are overlooked leads to the appointment of seven people to oversee the daily distribution, while the apostles attend to prayer and ministry of the word. Compare the practical attention to fairness, trusted responsibility, and distinct kinds of service. Acts describes an early Christian community’s response to a specific failure; it offers a comparison in organization without establishing the same institutional pattern as the Bahá’í passages.

subjects.displayTitle: Mind, soul, and body: one life, several languages
subjects.introduction: Search the brain and you will not find the intellect, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says, although the intellect is connected with the brain; love likewise has no place, yet it is bound to the heart. The puzzle of how an embodied person thinks, perceives, falls ill with fright or is cured by good news, and stays the same self while the body changes, is approached through homely relations: the lamp and its light, the tree and its fruit, the sun and its rays, the swordsman and the sword. Mind is the power of the spirit; the organs are its instruments; and in dreams the spirit sees without eyes and travels without feet. The vocabulary shifts, and that is part of the lesson: in one Tablet mind, soul and spirit are names for a single sign; elsewhere they are distinguished by function, and translators have not always kept the terms apart. Aristotle, defining soul as the form of a living body and illustrating it with the eye and its sight, gives another way to think about unity and distinction [1], while leaving open the question of independence the Bahá’í writings answer. Old remarks about deafness or illness judge no one’s understanding today. The way leads toward the human soul, its relationship to the body, and the connection between the material and spiritual worlds.
subjects.arc: Begin with mind and its images, compare the vocabulary of soul and spirit, examine embodied perception, and return to personal continuity.

order.why: Read the reported tree’s relation of seed and fruit.
Open with the distinction between connection and location.
shortened: The mind therefore has no place, although it is connected with the brain. So it is with the Kingdom. Likewise, love has no place, but it is connected with the heart.

order.why: Introduce the lamp, tree and sun as relational images.
shortened: As for the mind, it is the power of the human spirit. The spirit is as the lamp, and the mind as the light that shines from it. The spirit is as the tree, and the mind as the fruit. The mind is the perfection of the spirit and a necessary attribute thereof, even as the rays of the sun are an essential requirement of the sun itself.

order.why: Read the explanation of several names for one reality.
shortened: Know thou concerning what was asked about the mind, the soul and the spirit that these three and their like which are mentioned in reference to man are manifestations of that sign by which man was established.

For instance, that by which thou movest, hearest and seest is one, even if thou namest it by all names, as it has been called by different names by the tongues of those who remember. Yet in its essence it is sanctified above all that people speak of and all that they attribute to it. However, its manifestations and names differ according to the recipient and the means.

order.why: Compare functions assigned to spirit, mind and soul.
shortened: The spirit is the power of life, the mind is the power which apprehendeth the reality of things, and the soul is an intermediary between the Supreme Concourse (or Spiritual World) and the lower concourse (or material world).

order.why: Keep the reported vocabulary of soul, mind and bodily medium.
Explains connections between the bodily organs, mind and soul.
Read the reported distinctions of mental activity.
Compare heart and mind with their worldly and divine orientations.
Hear another reported use of heart and mind.
Examine the Forel Tablet’s distinction between changing faculties and soul.
shortened: Now concerning mental faculties, they are in truth of the inherent properties of the soul, even as the radiation of light is the essential property of the sun. The rays of the sun are renewed but the sun itself is ever the same and unchanged. Consider how the human intellect develops and weakens, and may at times come to naught, whereas the soul changeth not. For the mind to manifest itself, the human body must be whole; and a sound mind cannot be but in a sound body, whereas the soul dependeth not upon the body.

order.why: Consider coordination and interruption through the body.
shortened: And each one of these members hath its own special function. The mind force -- whether we call it pre-existent or contingent -- doth direct and co-ordinate all the members of the human body, seeing to it that each part or member duly performeth its own special function. If, however, there be some interruption in the power of the mind, all the members will fail to carry out their essential functions, deficiencies will appear in the body and the functioning of its members, and the power will prove ineffective.

order.why: Read the reported analogy of brain and mirror.
shortened: Question: What is meant by the Mirror for Divine Reflection?
Abdu'l Baha: "Mirror" is the whole body, the brain in particular.

order.why: Distinguish spatial location from connection in the reported account.
shortened: Intelligence does not partake of the quality of space, though it is related to man's brain. The intellect resides there, but not materially. Search in the brain you will not find the intellect. In the same way though the soul is a resident of the body it is not to be found in the body.

order.why: Hear the reported image of the brain as a throne.
shortened: The throne of reason is the brain. Reason is a monarch over the body and the five senses.

order.why: Read the reported connection of thought, brain and nerves.
Consider bodily organs as instruments of consciousness.
shortened: Know then that the spirit permeates and flows through all the members and organs of man, its will is effective, and the members and parts are its instruments, through which it manages affairs and arranges actions. The members are instruments and the spirit is the doer - like when someone takes up a sword and wages war: the sword is the instrument but is subject to the striker. The spirit sees through the eye, hears through the ear, speaks through the tongue, manages affairs through all the members, and all members are alive through the spirit.

order.why: Introduce the five outward senses.
Read the reported coordination of powers in memory.
Consider the reported distinction between sensory instruments and judgment.
Retain the historical report concerning sensory disability for contextual reading.
shortened: Among the prophets there have been some personages who were sightless, for instance Isaac, but there have been none who were deaf. Why? Because blindness is not a hindrance to gaining information, understanding, or discrimination, but deafness is, for he who is deaf cannot make others understand, nor can he himself understand clearly.

order.why: Keep the reported distinction between speed and thoughtfulness.
Read the reported account of sensation and intellection.
Consider the reported partnership of thought and bodily force.
Connect the rational soul with discovery.
Read the reported use of mind in relation to discovery.
shortened: The soul in itself cannot unravel the mysteries; but the mind is superior to the soul. The mind is a power whereby man can investigate the reality of every object. It unfolds to his vision the secrets of existence and leads him on and on to the station of divine sublimity. It frees man from the fetters of self and causes him to ascend to the pure heaven of sanctity.

order.why: Compare the further reported description of mind and soul.
shortened: There is, however, a faculty in man which unfolds to his vision the secrets of existence. It gives him a power whereby he may investigate the reality of every object. It leads man on and on to the luminous station of divine sublimity and frees him from all the fetters of self, causing him to ascend to the pure heaven of sanctity. This is the power of the mind, for the soul is not, of itself, capable of unrolling the mysteries of phenomena; but the mind can accomplish this and therefore it is a power superior to the soul.

order.why: Consider the perceiving soul’s discovery of realities.
shortened: The "perceiving soul" of man is the power which discovers. Wheresoever it is directed it discovers the hidden mysteries therein, and brings to light that which was veiled.

order.why: Distinguish intelligible realities from sensory objects.
shortened: The animals are keen in sensation, but man is endowed with piercing vision. Every moving creature apprehendeth sensible realities, but intelligible realities are disclosed and perceived by the seeing knower. Thus, among the inherent attributes of man and the infinite virtues of this noble species is the apprehension of intelligible, not sensible, realities; the discovery of unknown mysteries, not occupation with matters already known and seen.

order.why: Hear the reported relation between inner perception and reason.
shortened: Likewise, the outward faculties and senses of man discover and perceive the appearance of things. But the light of Intuition (or Inner Perception) is a light which comprehends the realities and the core of things. Intuition (or Inner Perception) means the Divine Universal Reason, and it comprehends and grasps supernatural things and conditions which cannot be grasped by the outward senses.

order.why: Introduce the limits of interpretation and reasoning.
shortened: The third criterion is that of tradition, that is, the text of the sacred scriptures, when it is said, "God said thus in the Torah," or "God said thus in the Gospel." This criterion is not perfect either, because the traditions must be understood by the mind. As the mind itself is liable to error, how can it be said that it will attain to perfect truth and not err in comprehending and inferring the meaning of the traditions?

order.why: Read the reported threefold image of intellectual light.
Consider the reported perception of what is unseen.
Compare inward meditation with outward sight.
Examine the account of spiritual activity through and beyond instruments.
shortened: The spirit has two modes of operation: one through instruments and means, that is, seeing through the eye, hearing through the ear, speaking through the tongue.

The other operation is without instruments, as in the world of dreams where one sees without eyes, hears without ears, speaks without tongue, and travels without moving the feet. All spiritual powers manifest without bodily means in the world of dreams.

order.why: Read sleep as an image of bodily rest and active spirit.
Consider the reported connection of heart and thought.
Keep the response about troubling thoughts within its reported question and answer.
shortened: Question: What is the source of evil thoughts that disturb those who do not wish to entertain them?  Answer: They come from other minds; they are reflected. One should not become a mirror for them--to reflect them; neither should one try to control them, for this is impossible; it only aggravates the difficulty, causing more to appear.

order.why: Hear the reported counsel concerning moods.
shortened: Be not the slave of your moods, but their master.

order.why: Read the examples of emotional and bodily interaction.
shortened: So for example when a sick person is suddenly given the good news that his most ardent wish and desire has been realized, a nervous excitement may result that will entirely dispel the ailment. In the same way, when a terrifying event suddenly comes to pass, such an excitement may be produced in the nerves of a healthy person that he immediately falls ill. The cause of the illness is not a material thing, for that person has not ingested or come into contact with anything: the nervous excitement alone has brought about the illness.

order.why: Keep the particular account of nerves and healing in historical context.
Consider the reported value of bodily health for expression.
Read the reported effect of deprivation on the mind.
Distinguish illness of the instrument from the soul in the reported account.
Consider the reported example of bodily pain.
Read the reported rider analogy and the influence of Christ after death.
Hear the reported connection of soul, body, virtue and memory.
Preserve the reported challenge to materialism as an argument to examine.
shortened: As soon as the atheist comes to you, as the great tempter and unifier and asks: "Prove, show to me your soul", then say to him boldly: "Prove to me that I have no soul, show me what it is that thinks in me, for the brain is but the implement, where is the life of the implement, where does the implement come from, who creates it?" - He will tell you: "As an honest person, as an upright seeker, I have to reply: "Nobody knows this, nobody can know this!"

order.why: Consider the reported image of waves in the sea of mind.
Close the linked passages with the reported relation of intellect and heart.
Retain the supplied explanation of variable terminology and personal identity.
shortened: But there is no doubt that spirit and soul seem to have been interchanged in meaning sometimes; soul and mind have, likewise, been interchanged in meaning, no doubt due to difficulties arising from different translations. What the Baha'is do believe though is that we have three aspects of our humanness, so to speak, a body, a mind and an immortal identity - soul or spirit. We believe the mind forms a link between the soul and the body, and the two interact on each other.

order.why: Close with the supplied notes distinguishing place from connection.

questions: Which image most helps you think about the relationship between mental life and bodily organs, and where does it become inadequate?
How do the meanings of mind, soul, spirit, and heart change across these passages?
What distinguishes a claim about the soul’s existence from an account of how perception or memory operates?
How can historical statements about health or disability be examined while honoring the experience and understanding of people today?
What does Aristotle’s relation of form and body clarify, and how does it differ from the mirror and reflected sun?
What questions about personal continuity become more important when bodily capacities change?

references.label: 1 · Aristotle, On the Soul II.1 · Form and living body
references.note: In J. A. Smith’s translation, Aristotle defines soul as the actuality or form of an organized body capable of life. His eye and sight example explores the unity of a living capacity with its organ. Compare this with the compilation’s images of instruments and reflected light. Aristotle leaves qualifications about separability at the end of the chapter; his account should not be treated as a simple equivalent of the Bahá’í argument for the soul’s independence.

subjects.introduction: Sulphur, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells a seeker, is the fire of the love of God, and mercury the quicksilver of the knowledge of God; combine the two and you hold the philosopher’s stone, the elixir that turns the copper and iron of souls into gold. Alchemy in the Bahá’í writings begins and ends in the heart. Yet Bahá’u’lláh, pressed by questioners, also answered with detailed accounts of the hidden craft itself, its elements and operations, and then forbade His followers to pursue it, calling the practice a waste of life whose hour had not come. That hour, He said, belongs to the coming of age of the human race, and its arrival will bring peril as well as power. The question underneath is what a transformation is for, and what becomes of the person who seeks it. Malachi’s refiner, purifying silver so that worship may be made righteous, offers a kindred image of purification [1]. The road from here leads toward the maturity of mankind, the ancient wisdom of Hermes, and the transmutation of the soul by the divine elixir.
subjects.arc: Begin with spiritual transformation and the explicit counsels about pursuit, then read the historical language of the craft and its relation to maturity.

order.why: Distinguish the specialized names and the direction given to believers.
shortened: As to what thou hast asked concerning the honored stone - whether it be copper or lead or something else - know thou that it hath been called by all names, but most people understand not.

We do not desire that any of the loved ones occupy themselves with it. Rather, it behooveth thee and those who have believed to make your chief concern in these days the remembrance of God and the promotion of His decisive and wise Cause. His love is verily the supreme elixir and the most glorious crown, whereby the base metals of hearts are transformed into pure gold.

order.why: Open with love and knowledge as the elixir of changed souls.
shortened: O thou servant of the True One! Sulphur is the fire of the love of God, and mercury is the quicksilver of the ocean of the knowledge of God. Combine then these twin noble elements, and harmonize and unite these twin soundest pillars, and so obtain the Noblest Stone---that is, the Jewel of Jewels, the Ruby of the Mine of the Kingdom---so that thou mayest discover the Most Great Elixir and find the Alchemy of Truth, and, casting it upon the copper and iron of men’s souls, transmute them into purest gold.

order.why: Read the retort of the heart and the fire of love.
Consider the Word’s transforming power.
shortened: O Wise One! Has the crown of victory such power as to transform diverse elements in a single thing and bring them to the station of pure gold? Though such transformation appears difficult and complex, yet the transformation of earthly power to heavenly power is possible in the sight of this Wronged One. That which effects this transformation is greater than the elixir. This station and this power are specific to the Word of God.

order.why: Establish the explicit prohibition and the statement about an appointed time.
shortened: In regard to what thou hast asked about the craft, this Wronged One hath not, of His own accord, set forth anything on this subject. However, certain individuals have asked questions, and, in response, the Pen of the Most High set down the explanations that are found in the Tablets.

Nevertheless, its appearance hath been made one of the signs of the coming of age of the human race, and the time when this shall happen hath been fixed. As yet it hath not come, but when it cometh it shall be manifested through the power of Him Who is the Sovereign Truth. He, verily, is the All-Informed, the All-Knowing. For this reason all have been prohibited from becoming engaged with it. None hath the right to busy himself therewith.

order.why: Read the explanation that questions prompted the discussions.
shortened: As to what was written concerning the elixir, this Most Exalted Word was repeatedly heard from the tongue of the Lord of Names - exalted be His utterance and mighty His proof: "O servant in attendance! Whatever hath been revealed concerning the elixir from the heaven of divine Will was in response to the questions of the servants. They repeatedly asked until that which was revealed was revealed. Otherwise, the Most Exalted Pen would not have addressed it and hath not had, nor hath, any inclination to mention such matters.

order.why: Keep the response concerning prohibition and wasted effort.
shortened: This servant heard repeatedly from the Blessed Tongue saying that had the questioners not attributed it to incapacity or worse, surely no word would have been revealed concerning it, and repeatedly did He forbid the servants from practicing it - a mighty prohibition in the Book. As commanded, thou and the trustees of the Cause should wisely and with utterance prevent the friends of Truth from engaging in this pursuit which is in truth a waste of life.

order.why: Read the related account under its separate source identity.
shortened: Regarding what you wrote about one of the friends of God expressing grief over the believers' involvement with the craft of elixir-making, verily he hath spoken the truth. Indeed, right is with him in prohibiting this act. Multiple Tablets have been revealed from the heaven of divine Will and sent to various regions concerning this. It is most strange that despite clear prohibition, they engage in this futile pursuit.

order.why: Consider the warning about distraction through these pursuits.
Hear the reported warning concerning pretensions to the process.
Retain the polemical account of fruitless pursuit.
Read the detailed answer beside its renewed prohibition.
shortened: However, some petitions from before and after arrived from various directions inquiring about this matter. Therefore, in response to each one, as was befitting, drops from the ocean of knowledge were manifested, and whenever anyone wished to engage in this pursuit, they were forbidden and told that the time had not yet come - wait until God brings it forth in His Own time. For today all must be focused on another matter, which is teaching the souls with wisdom and utterance, so that the copper of the existence of the servants might be transformed into pure gold through the elixir of the divine Word and that they turn toward the supreme horizon.
We have not given leave to anyone to occupy himself with this matter. To this testifieth My tongue and My pen and beyond them thy Lord, the All-Knowing, the All-Informed.

order.why: Consider concealment, world order and the enduring craft of hearts.
shortened: Rather, the purpose was that this hidden secret and guarded mystery remained concealed in the days of the Holy Manifestations. Its disclosure is not permitted now, for the order of the world would be disrupted and affairs would become disordered.

Now observe this - that the Holy Manifestations did not address such matters. It is certain that the hand of divine infallibility is upon this, otherwise by now it would have been the secret of every gathering and the minaret of every assembly.

Therefore seek you the ancient treasure and desire the mighty influence, so that brilliant traces may encompass all horizons. This is the enduring craft, this is the eternal gift, this is the penetrating elixir in hearts and spirits, this is the illuminator of forms.

order.why: Read the warning against squandering resources.
Examine the Book of Certitude’s examples and its challenge to pretended learning.
shortened: For instance, consider the substance of copper. Were it to be protected in its own mine from becoming solidified, it would, within the space of seventy years, attain to the state of gold. There are some, however, who maintain that copper itself is gold, which by becoming solidified is in a diseased condition, and hath not therefore reached its own state.

Among the sciences which this pretender hath professed is that of alchemy. We cherish the hope that either a king or a man of preeminent power may call upon him to translate this science from the realm of fancy to the domain of fact and from the plane of mere pretension to that of actual achievement.

order.why: Read the argument concerning transmutation and divine power.
shortened: “Is it ever possible,” they ask, “for gold to be transmuted into copper?” Say, Yes, by my Lord, it is possible. Its secret, however, lieth hidden in Our Knowledge. We will reveal it unto whom We will. Whoso doubteth Our power, let him ask the Lord his God, that He may disclose unto him the secret, and assure him of its truth. That copper can be turned into gold is in itself sufficient proof that gold can, in like manner, be transmuted into copper, if they be of them that can apprehend this truth. Every mineral can be made to acquire the density, form, and substance of each and every other mineral. The knowledge thereof is with Us in the Hidden Book.

order.why: Consider the extended answer about corruption, gold and dust.
shortened: But even should it be so, we say, in the first place: this incapacity belongeth indeed to the realm of the contingent; yet God is powerful over all things. He transformeth whatsoever He willeth. Should He desire to turn the gold of the world into copper, He is free to do so, and able; and if He willeth, He createth the possibility of change in all things by His command, and then altereth them by His sovereignty; verily He is the All-Powerful, the Almighty.

Moreover, the sages have declared that gold, if it remain in earth for a time, is changed into earth. But apart from the sayings of the philosophers, there is the saying of God Himself: "All have I created from dust, and unto dust will I return them." It is therefore established that gold becometh dust; and dust---most certainly---is baser than copper.

order.why: Keep the Tablet of Wisdom’s account of Socrates in its historical setting.
Distinguish physical balanced nature from spiritual reality.
Introduce the distinction between absolute power and harmonious combination.
shortened: Listen with pure and sanctified hearing. Be not distressed at the delay of matters - every matter is bound to its time.

In the mixing and combination of things, two stations are to be considered: one through pure absolute power, and this depends on His leave and is specific to His presence; the other through the conjunction of harmonious things that are not mutually repellent, and this, after knowledge of the perfect nature, is known among the philosophers as "the egg," and it is the fashioned stone, containing the four natures, and after separation is capable of complete mixture.

order.why: Hear the reported example of decomposition and composition.
Read the account of the four elements with its concluding spiritual direction.
shortened: In brief, what is intended by the hidden craft is that thou shouldst separate the four elements from a single thing, and after purifying each element from incidental impurities through dissolution and coagulation, unite these elements.

In these days that which is beloved and desired is that thou shouldst take somewhat of the active essence, which is love for the Servant of God, and place it upon the conflicting elements of the human temple, so that all may be cleansed, through the assistance of that Most Great Essence, from the dross of earthly realms and enter the eternal kingdom.

order.why: Consider the response concerning Maria, knowledge before practice, and peril.
shortened: When thou dost purpose to pursue this hidden art, first ponder and reflect whether this supreme craft exists, or whether, like the Simurgh and Phoenix of old, it is but a name without reality.

The manifestation of this hidden treasure among these people is a sign of the world's maturity, after which shall follow grave peril and barren tribulation for the world and its people, unless all enter the divine paradise.
O seeker! Hearken unto the counsel of this imprisoned servant. Act not before knowledge, and seek not from other than the source.

order.why: Read the many names and qualities attributed to the stone.
shortened: As to what thou hast asked concerning the Stone, know thou that it lieth scattered in every place, and within it We have ordained treasures that none knoweth save him whom We have taught knowledge from Our presence. Verily thy Lord is the All-Knowing, the All-Informed. It is one in itself yet from it appear multiplicities. Blessed is he who recognizeth it and witnesseth therein the power of God, and whom nothing preventeth from this straight path. It is God's treasure among His servants, the repository of mysteries among His creation, and the dawning-place of power to every discerning one who seeth.

order.why: Examine the extended account of separation, oil and water.
shortened: Now observe that some people suppose that the stone exists and countless differences appear concerning it - each group considers some thing to be the stone and busies itself with treating it, wasting their lives. This is why they have said "Work comes after knowledge." In any case, the stone has been and will be hidden, stored, and concealed.

However, repeatedly it was heard from the Most Holy Tongue that due to the questions of some friends, the Supreme Pen became occupied and spoke concerning this science, though He did not wish the friends to become occupied with it, and He has mentioned the reason for this in some Tablets.

order.why: Read the stages of purification and union in the alchemical vocabulary.
shortened: First, one must know wherein the All-Wise Lord and All-Knowing Sovereign hath placed this mighty matter and sublime mystery. Then must one purify and sanctify the soul and spirit from the cage of self and desire, that it may become worthy of this divine trust and heavenly artifice.

Take then the luminous water from the dark fire, that the high may be distinguished from the low, and separation be made between water and earth. After separation, let purification occur that it may be fit for marriage and mixture.

order.why: Keep the particular instruction concerning fire and reflection.
Follow the symbolism of water, light and renewed life.
shortened: By God, this is from the philosophers' gold about which souls have wandered and the minds of the wise have been bewildered, and until now none has attained it except servants whom the ornaments of the world do not distract from the remembrance of God, the All-Compelling, the Self-Subsisting.

This is the soul and blood and the red resin, whereby decaying bodies are brought to life when this spirit is breathed into them. Therefore, O ye people of the Art, seek after it! But attend to the fire, and apply it not in such measure as would harm it, for fire both corrupts and perfects, were ye but to perceive it.

order.why: Read the Commentary on Hú’s combination of material and theological language.
shortened: And if thou shouldst follow this principle which We have mentioned to thee in all the ranks of knowledge concerning minerals and plants, after turning unto God and achieving extinction in Him and subsistence through Him, thou shalt attain unto that which God hath intended for thee through the hidden treasures of His knowledge and the stored mysteries of His wisdom. For this principle is among the principles that have encompassed all possibility in their essence and all creation in their form, for the Cause is naught but separation and union. And if thou art able to separate all that is in the heavens and earth, and unite them all after purification until they become one thing, the mysteries of this mighty secret shall be made manifest unto thee.

order.why: Hear the Báb’s account of conditions, effects and divine permission.
shortened: The science of elixir, like the creation of all things, hath neither beginning nor end - a knowledge that God hath concealed behind holy veils, and when He bestoweth it upon any of His servants, they act by God's command. And what the seekers of guidance say manifesteth no effect until the Effector permitteth it from Our presence. Say: Glory be to God! At the time of effect, God hath already permitted it - do ye not see?

order.why: Read the Báb’s fourfold description of materials and operations.
shortened: Look first to the hidden knowledge which is the essence of all sciences, for its pillars are four: Western Mercury, which is cold and moist; Eastern Yellow Water, which is hot and moist; Eastern Red Water, which is hot and dry; and the purified weight known as the iron body and sacred earth, which is cold and dry. Also, all its operations are four: First, the separation of matter; second, the marriage, through which the precious stone is completed; third, the separation of pillars and natures; and fourth, the combination of pillars, and at this stage the elixir is completed and appears in the garment of excellence, demolishing ranks and caring not for thousands.

order.why: Preserve the distinctive terminology of this account of the hidden craft.
shortened: And verily in this station of thine take the tree of Sinai from the head of the youth, then wash it at the boundary of Safa, then take its water four times. When thou hast taken the fifth water it must needs be a thin yellow. Then preserve it and take oil from the fourth oil of sulfur after leaving it from the first part from the first water, and likewise similar to the first. When it reacheth the boundary of seven, the Name of God, the Living, shall be made manifest. Cast it according to the measure thou wishest from God's outpouring, for I find no cessation in the outpouring of God.

order.why: Follow the Báb’s relation of elixir, divine signs and mineral realm.
shortened: As to thy question regarding the Elixir, know thou that God hath created nothing but that He hath placed within it the Letter of the Elixir in its appointed station.

Fire -- this is the Greatest Name of God: kindle it to unveil the veils of benefits. Then set the branch upon its proper limit that it may put forth growth; and take of the fruit of the Tree that issued from Mount Sinai, according to the measure of Decree in the secret of Destiny, and carry it to its place: thou shalt find the Oil of the Greatest Red. Thereupon the fire shall be nearer than the twinkling of an eye.

order.why: Keep the letter’s technical allusions in their own terms.
Read the alembic and ascent in a cosmological image.
Consider the Báb’s image of extracting components from human hearts.
shortened: O Ali! We have appointed the alembic and retort from the beginning of this Cause among Our servants that We might extract the elixiric components from the hearts of those who desire naught but God and are thankful unto Him.
And all that God hath created in the kingdoms of heaven and earth and what lieth between them is contained within this temple - the temple of man. Will ye not then be thankful?

order.why: Uses the elixir as an image of the transforming power of the divine Word.
Hear the reported reflection on unintended useful discoveries.
Introduce the two signs of humanity’s coming of age.
Keep the explanation that their meaning remains veiled.
Read the association of maturity, peace and hidden wisdom.
Hear the reported parallel account of world maturity.
Consider the unifying influence of a concealed power.
Close the linked passages with the elixir of love.
Retain the supplied letter’s interpretation of possible material conditions.
Keep the supplied pilgrim notes and their historical account of matter.
shortened: One thing can never of itself change into another; but by changing the surrounding conditions and combining it with something else it can be changed.... The way has not yet been discovered in Europe - but when the method is discovered it will be possible to change copper into gold, or to change the nature of metals - the time for this discovery is not yet.

order.why: Read the supplied statement of transforming power.
Close with the supplied Hermetic image of above and below.

questions: How does the opening account of love and knowledge change the question of what should be transformed?
Which passages clearly use spiritual imagery, and which leave questions about a material craft?
How do the explicit prohibitions shape your reading of the detailed descriptions?
What relationship appears between the acquisition of power and the maturity needed to use it?
How does Malachi’s purification of worship compare with the transformation of character described here?
What would count as fruitful knowledge in your own life, and what pursuits might consume effort without bringing that fruit?

references.label: 1 · Malachi 3:1–4 · Refining and righteousness
references.note: The coming messenger introduces an image of refining silver and gold, applied to the purification of the sons of Levi so that their offerings become righteous. Compare that moral and religious use of metallurgy with the compilation’s spiritual elixir. Malachi’s setting is the renewal of priestly worship; the connection is the work of purification, without identifying refining with alchemical transmutation or treating the passages as the same teaching.

subjects.displayTitle: Acquiring knowledge: discovery with a purpose
subjects.introduction: Whoever thirsts for knowledge, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says, lives in the schools even while sitting at home, taking a word from every book and a lesson from every scholar met along the way, and the time for such learning runs from the beginning of life to its end. Bahá’u’lláh calls knowledge wings for a person’s life and a ladder for ascent, and lays its acquisition on everyone, young and old, men and women alike. Yet He also asks a hard question at the outset of every study: where does it lead, and whom does it profit? Learning that begins and ends in words is set aside; learning that lifts the condition of people is the very pride of a nation. The rational soul, patiently investigating, draws hidden realities out of the invisible into the light. Confucius pairs study with thought and counts knowing what one does not know as knowledge too [1]. From here the road runs toward the four methods by which knowledge is gained, the high station of the arts and sciences, and the promise of universal education.
subjects.arc: Begin with lifelong curiosity, connect knowledge with human benefit, examine discovery, and bring the inquiry into shared education and practice.

order.why: Consider knowledge as joy, ascent and benefit to the world.
shortened: Knowledge is as wings to man's life, and a ladder for his ascent. Its acquisition is incumbent upon everyone. The knowledge of such sciences, however, should be acquired as can profit the peoples of the earth, and not those which begin with words and end with words.
In truth, knowledge is a veritable treasure for man, and a source of glory, of bounty, of joy, of exaltation, of cheer and gladness unto him.

order.why: Open with the learner whose true dwelling is in schools.
shortened: One who thirsts for knowledge - his education is not limited by boundaries. Though he may be at home, his true nest and dwelling is in reality in the schools, for day and night he strives to obtain a word from every book and memorize a phrase from every treatise, and studies it deeply, and from every scholar he encounters, he seeks explanation of those questions. It is certain that ultimately he will become a peerless scholar and an unequaled learned one.

order.why: Hear the reported invitation to learn throughout life.
Read the reported palace of the mind furnished by many kinds of thought.
Ground arts and sciences in reflection and human well-being.
shortened: O people of Baha! The source of crafts, sciences and arts is the power of reflection. Make ye every effort that out of this ideal mine there may gleam forth such pearls of wisdom and utterance as will promote the well-being and harmony of all the kindreds of the earth.

order.why: Read social good as the honor of learning.
shortened: The happiness and pride of a nation consist in this, that it should shine out like the sun in the high heaven of knowledge. "Shall they who have knowledge and they who have it not, be treated alike?" And the honor and distinction of the individual consist in this, that he among all the world's multitudes should become a source of social good. Is any larger bounty conceivable than this, that an individual, looking within himself, should find that by the confirming grace of God he has become the cause of peace and well-being, of happiness and advantage to his fellow men?

order.why: Examine the test of consequences and useful knowledge.
shortened: At the outset of every endeavour, it is incumbent to look to the end of it.  Of all the arts and sciences, set the children to studying those which will result in advantage to man, will ensure his progress and elevate his rank.

The Great Being saith:  The learned of the day must direct the people to acquire those branches of knowledge which are of use, that both the learned themselves and the generality of mankind may derive benefits therefrom.  Such academic pursuits as begin and end in words alone have never been and will never be of any worth.

order.why: Keep the permission and direction toward beneficial study.
Read the approval of diminishing ignorance.
shortened: Verily I say, whatsoever leadeth to the decline of ignorance and the increase of knowledge hath been, and will ever remain, approved in the sight of the Lord of creation.

order.why: Hear the universal duty to acquire knowledge.
Connect learning with the expansion of consciousness.
shortened: There are certain pillars which have been established as the unshakeable supports of the Faith of God. The mightiest of these is learning and the use of the mind, the expansion of consciousness, and insight into the realities of the universe and the hidden mysteries of Almighty God.
To promote knowledge is thus an inescapable duty imposed on every one of the friends of God.

order.why: Join outward and inward perfections.
shortened: O friends! Strive to acquire knowledge and wisdom, and exert mighty efforts to gain both outer and inner perfections.

order.why: Read the fruitful tree of human capacities.
shortened: Strive diligently to acquire both outward and inward perfections, for the fruit of the human tree has ever been outer and inner perfections.
Therefore you must needs adorn, according to your capacity and means, the tree of your being with the fruits of knowledge and wisdom, of meanings and utterance.

order.why: Keep knowledge together with gentleness and love.
Consider learning across age and gender, in gatherings and individual effort.
shortened: Therefore, the friends of God, young and old, men and women, must strive to the extent possible to acquire sciences and knowledge, increase their understanding of the mysteries of the Holy Books, and gain proficiency in presenting divine proofs and evidences.

Now too, I earnestly implore the friends of God to strive as much as possible - the more they strive to expand the scope of education, the better and sweeter it will become - so that the friends of God, whether young or old, male or female, may each strive according to their capacity to acquire sciences, knowledge and current arts, both spiritual and material. In their gatherings, let all discuss scientific matters and become informed of the sciences and knowledge of the age.

order.why: Hear the reported call for education suited to people’s needs.
Read basic literacy as a common foundation.
Consider encouragement that widens access to useful learning.
Imagine schoolchildren becoming learned adults.
Read the aspiration addressed to young people.
Keep the particular call to learn for the advancement of Iran.
Retain the personal encouragement to two brothers.
Bring sciences, poetry and composition into a course of study.
shortened: You had asked about my wish - my purpose is that you study the sciences and knowledge, acquire the art of poetry and composition, complete your studies in school, raise the call to the Kingdom, and engage in spreading the lights of truth.

order.why: Consider active contribution to inventions and arts.
shortened: Be ye in that land vanguards of the perfections of humankind; carry forward the various branches of knowledge, be active and progressive in the field of inventions and the arts.

order.why: Hear the reported program of education, science and the removal of social evils.
shortened: First; Whole-hearted service to the Cause of education, the unfolding of the mysteries of nature, the extension of the boundaries of Pure Science, the elimination of the causes of ignorance and social evils, the standardization of a universal system of instruction, and the diffusion of the lights of knowledge and reality.

order.why: Read the purpose of learning through service, inclusion and hope.
shortened: Wherefore, O ye illumined youth, strive by night and by day to unravel the mysteries of the mind and spirit, and to grasp the secrets of the Day of God.

Lead those who thirst to the fountain of life; grant ye true health to the ailing. Be ye apprentices of God; be ye physicians directed by God and heal ye the sick among humankind. Bring those who have been excluded into the circle of intimate friends. Make the despairing to be filled with hope. Waken them that slumber; make the heedless mindful.
Such are the fruits of this earthly life. Such is the station of resplendent glory.

order.why: Connect the reported cultivation of mind with durable relationships.
shortened: First of all, be ready to sacrifice your lives for one another, to prefer the general well-being to your personal well-being. Create relationships that nothing can shake; form an assembly that nothing can break up; have a mind that never ceases acquiring riches that nothing can destroy.

order.why: Consider the reported importance of inner development for human improvement.
shortened: The important factor in human improvement is the mind. In the world of the mind there must needs be development and improvement. There must be reformation in the kingdom of the human spirit; otherwise, no result will be attained from betterment of the mere physical structure.

order.why: Introduce discovery through the Forel Tablet.
Read the movement from hidden knowledge to visible achievement.
shortened: All that you observe of crafts, wonders, effects and discoveries was once in the realm of the unseen and was a hidden matter. The human spirit discovered that hidden secret and brought it from the realm of the unseen to the world of being.

order.why: Consider the distinctive discovering power.
Examine the movement from known realities to what is unknown.
shortened: This spirit is the discovering power that encompasses all things. All the wondrous signs, all the crafts and discoveries, all the mighty undertakings and momentous historical events of which you are aware have been discovered by this spirit and brought forth from the invisible realm into the visible plane through its spiritual power. Thus it abides upon the earth and yet makes discoveries in the heavens, and deduces that which is unknown from known and visible realities.

order.why: Read the scope and limit of investigating contingent things.
shortened: Through the power of the rational soul man can discover the realities of things, comprehend their properties and penetrate the mysteries of existence. All the sciences, branches of learning, arts, inventions, institutions, undertakings and discoveries have resulted from the comprehension of the rational soul. These were once impenetrable secrets, hidden mysteries and unknown realities, and the rational soul gradually discovered them and brought them out of the invisible plane into the realm of the visible. This is the greatest power of comprehension in the world of nature, and the uttermost limit of its flight is to comprehend the realities, signs and properties of contingent things.

order.why: Emphasize the gradual work of discovery.
shortened: For instance, all the existing crafts, inventions, sciences, and branches of learning have been discovered by the human reality. At one time they were all hidden and concealed mysteries, but the reality of man gradually discovered them and brought them forth from the invisible world into the visible realm.

order.why: Hear the reported praise of intellectual investigation.
Read the reported language of revealing nature’s hidden secrets.
Compare another reported account of bringing hidden arts to light.
Keep the reported relation between knowledge and spiritual progress.
shortened: The intelligence of man, his reasoning powers, his knowledge, his scientific achievements, all these being manifestations of the spirit, partake of the inevitable law of spiritual progress and are, therefore, of necessity, immortal.

order.why: Read the explicit encouragement to study philosophy.
Consider the Word’s different fruits in receptive minds.
shortened: The Sun of Truth is the Word of God, upon which dependeth the education of those who are endowed with the power of understanding and of utterance.

Its appearance in every mirror is conditioned by the colour of that mirror. For instance, when its light is cast upon the mirrors of the hearts of the wise, it bringeth forth wisdom. In like manner, when it manifesteth itself in the mirrors of the hearts of craftsmen, it unfoldeth new and unique arts, and when reflected in the hearts of those that apprehend the truth, it revealeth wondrous tokens of true knowledge and discloseth the verities of God’s utterance.

order.why: Read creativity through the divine name.
Connect learning with spiritual orientation.
shortened: It is incumbent upon thee to acquire the various branches of knowledge, and to turn thy face toward the beauty of the Manifest Beauty, that thou mayest be a sign of saving guidance amongst the peoples of the world, and a focal center of understanding in this sphere from which the wise and their wisdom are shut out, except for those who set foot in the Kingdom of lights and become informed of the veiled and hidden mystery, the well-guarded secret.

order.why: Hear the call to sustained effort in sciences and arts.
shortened: Ye must therefore put forth a mighty effort, striving by night and day and resting not for a moment, to acquire an abundant share of all the sciences and arts, that the Divine Image, which shineth out from the Sun of Truth, may illumine the mirror of the hearts of men.

order.why: Read the teacher of love in the school of truth.
shortened: Therefore you must not rest or be still day or night, engage in acquiring divine knowledge, and in the school of truth learn lessons from the teacher of love so that you may become the cause of consolation to these yearning ones.

order.why: Keep the reported pairing of modern learning and spiritual civilization.
Hear the invitation to become a fountain of knowledge.
shortened: Become fountains of knowledge and learning, and the wise ones of the world of grace and insight.

order.why: Urges diligent study and excellence in sciences and arts.
Read the brief counsel toward advancement.
Close the linked passages with the reported hope for ever-growing understanding.
shortened: My hope for you is that as you travel through the universe of existence you will ever become acquainted with new and wonderful significances; that your knowledge will ever be increased - knowledge without limitation; then you will understand the realities existing in all kingdoms.

order.why: Retain the supplied account of perceiving and cooperating with hidden law.
Keep the supplied provisional invitation to methodical investigation.
Read the supplied account of learning as a duty of humanity.
shortened: To promote learning, to propagate education and all the branches of useful knowledge, to encourage the spread of information as to the secrets of creation, to decipher the codes that are hidden away in the inmost core of all things, to study sciences that are beneficial and learn to unravel the secrets of the earth and to conquer the very summits of the mysteries of the universe - not only are these among the binding and inescapable duties of humankind, but in these lie the primary means whereby man can continually go forward and prosper. Expressly stated in the Divine Texts is this, that the greatest encouragement must be given to such pursuits.

order.why: Close with the supplied encouragement to acquire advanced knowledge.

questions: What kind of learning has enlarged both your understanding and your ability to help others?
How broadly should the usefulness of knowledge be understood, especially in the arts or basic research?
What does the image of bringing hidden realities into view suggest about curiosity and patient investigation?
How can a community make learning available across differences of age, opportunity, and prior education?
What do the Analects’ counsels about reflection and admitting ignorance add to the enthusiasm expressed here?
Which field would you like to explore next, and how might your manner of learning embody both rigor and generosity?

references.label: 1 · Confucius, Analects 2.15 and 2.17 · Thought and intellectual honesty
references.note: In Part 2 of this translation, Confucius pairs study with reflection and defines knowledge to include acknowledging what one does not know. Compare those habits with the compilation’s enthusiasm for discovery and useful learning. These short counsels concern the formation of a thoughtful person; the Bahá’í passages additionally connect learning with revelation, universal education, and the advancement of civilization.

subjects.displayTitle: Astronomy: wonder in an open universe
subjects.introduction: A boy once sat through a lecture on the old Ptolemaic heavens, the earth wrapped in crystal spheres like the layers of an onion, and came away miserable, feeling himself a prisoner inside them; days later a line of Bahá’u’lláh’s about infinite space set him free. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá told that story about Himself, and it holds the whole mood of this subject. The sky in the Writings is open: each fixed star has its planets, each planet is a world, their number outruns every enumerator, and the science that studies them is called a fathomless ocean whose discoveries are far from finished. Bahá’u’lláh explains that the seven heavens of earlier scripture spoke to the understanding of their age, while the Báb reads the spots on the moon as signs with an inner meaning, so a reader learns to tell observation from analogy and from interpretation. Psalm 8 looks at the same moon and stars and asks why so small a creature should be remembered at all [1]. The wonder leads onward into the nature of light and of ether, into infinity and eternity, and into the pervasiveness of life in the cosmos.
